chapter_title: The Chapter of Fasting, for it engenders a Host of Angels
chapter_note: This chapter contains zero substrate material. Teaching purity is 0.000 — no cosmological-correspondential vocabulary appears anywhere. The entire chapter is a narrative about a Manichaean archegos (church leader) who asks Mani to release him from institutional responsibilities (overseeing fasting of fifty elect, counting angels engendered). Mani refuses and encourages him to continue church-building. Content is exclusively institutional: fasting arithmetic, lord's days, elect/catechumen distinction, church construction, alms, preaching vs. individual edification. The seven-angels-per-fast doctrine is Manichaean institutional theology (Augustine confirms this in Conf. III.18), not pre-Mani correspondential teaching. The chapter is heavily damaged in §5-6 and scattered lacunae throughout. No extraction possible — no oldest teaching layer present.

Direct institutional charge: continue the proclaimed work, benefit comes in your lifetime. 'Do not strive to ask exemption from it' — administrative command. Partially damaged but clearly institutional counsel.

Key institutional teaching: the one who preaches and builds the church has greater glory than the brother who only edifies himself. Institutional score 3.92. This is a doctrine about institutional vocation vs. individual contemplation — entirely ecclesiastical.

Addresses the disciple's specific fear about sin when commanding church-building or alms. Institutional score 8.64 — highest among the response paragraphs. Direct institutional commission: 'I assign to you this alone: Have you power to preach and to build the church of God, for your toil will be reckoned to your benefit.' Institutional score 6.67. Clear administrative appointment formula.
